from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w,h = im.size
cols=[]
for x in range(w):
    rs=gs=bs=0
    for y in range(h):
        r,g,b = im.getpixel((x,y))
        rs+=r; gs+=g; bs+=b
    cols.append((rs//h, gs//h, bs//h))
# Segment: group consecutive columns with similar color
def dist(a,b): return abs(a[0]-b[0])+abs(a[1]-b[1])+abs(a[2]-b[2])
segs=[]
start=0
ref=cols[0]
for x in range(1,w):
    if dist(cols[x], ref) > 18:
        segs.append((start, x-1, ref))
        start=x; ref=cols[x]
    else:
        # slowly update ref
        ref = tuple((ref[i]*3+cols[x][i])//4 for i in range(3))
segs.append((start, w-1, ref))
print('num segments:', len(segs))
for s,e,c in segs:
    width=e-s+1
    print(f'{s:4d}-{e:4d} w={width:3d} rgb={c}')
"

from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w,h = im.size
px = im.load()
# Check whether columns are uniform vertically and find exact stripe boundaries
diffs=[]
for x in range(w-1):
    d = max(max(abs(px[x,y][i]-px[x+1,y][i]) for i in range(3)) for y in range(h))
    diffs.append(d)
# Exact-equality boundaries
exact=[x for x in range(w-1) if all(px[x,y]==px[x+1,y] for y in range(h))]
print('identical-adjacent columns at:', exact[:20], '...total', len(exact))
# boundaries where columns differ
big=[x for x in range(w-1) if diffs[x]>0]
print('columns where any diff:', len(big))
# vertical uniformity: max vertical diff within a column
vmax=[]
for x in range(0,w,100):
    d=0
    for y in range(h-1):
        d=max(d, max(abs(px[x,y][i]-px[x,y+1][i]) for i in range(3)))
    vmax.append((x,d))
print('vertical uniformity samples:', vmax)
"

input.command:
python3 -c "
from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w,h = im.size
px = im.load()
# Sample the color at the center of every 4px block (250 stripes)
colors=[]
for i in range(250):
    x = min(i*4+2, w-1)
    colors.append(px[x,0])
import math
def lum(c): return 0.2126*c[0]+0.7152*c[1]+0.0722*c[2]
def name(c):
    r,g,b=c
    if lum(c)<15: return 'black'
    mx,mn=max(c),min(c)
    sat=(mx-mn)/max(mx,1)
    if sat<0.15: return 'gray/white' if lum(c)>90 else 'gray-dark'
    if b>r and b>g: return 'BLUE' if b>40 else 'blue-dark'
    if r>g and g>b:
        if r>80 and g>55: return 'tan/bright-warm'
        if r>40: return 'brown'
        return 'dark-warm'
    if r>g and b>g: return 'purple/magenta'
    return 'other'
print('i  pct  rgb  lum  label')
for i,c in enumerate(colors):
    pct = i/250*100
    print(f'{i:3d} {pct:5.1f} {c} {lum(c):6.1f} {name(c)}')
" | head -130

part.text:
Now I have a full color map. Key features of this barcode:

- **Very dark overall** (mean luminance 26.6; 57% of stripes have luminance <25; only 4% >60)
- Opens with **dark blue** stripes (0–1%), then warm browns
- Bright **tan/brown** sections at ~9–11%, ~25–29%, ~40–46%, ~65–68%
- A **bright gray/white** flash at ~32% (lum 109)
- **Deep blue AND deep red** dark stripes at ~50–54% (alternating)
- Dark blue again at ~87–88%
- A **long, very steady dark-brown** run at ~89–98.5%, then fade to black

"**Let Her Go**" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter [Passenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passenger_\(singer\) "Passenger (singer)"). It was recorded at [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney")'s [Linear Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_Recording "Linear Recording") and co-produced by Passenger (as Mike Rosenberg) and Chris Vallejo. The recording features Australian musicians Stu Larsen, [Georgia Mooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Mooney "Georgia Mooney"), [Stu Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stu_Hunter "Stu Hunter"), Cameron Undy, and Glenn Wilson. "Let Her Go" was released on 24 July 2012 as the second single from Passenger's fourth album, *[All the Little Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Little_Lights "All the Little Lights")*.

The song became a [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit"), achieving international success and topping the charts in many countries around the world. As of July 2014, it has sold over one million digital copies in the UK, and over four million in the US.[\[1\]](#cite_note-uksales-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-USSales-2) In 2014, the song was nominated for the [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award") for [British Single of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_BRIT_Awards#Nominees_and_winners "2014 BRIT Awards"), and won Passenger the British Academy's [Ivor Novello Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Award "Ivor Novello Award") for Most Performed Work.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) In 2023, to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the song, Passenger released a remix version with English singer [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran").

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Passenger.jpg/250px-Passenger.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Passenger.jpg)

Passenger performing "Let Her Go" live in [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogotá "Bogotá"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") during his [Runaway Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_Tour_\(Passenger\) "Runaway Tour (Passenger)").

"Let Her Go" was released in July 2012 as the second single from Passenger's third album *[All the Little Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Little_Lights "All the Little Lights")*. The song became a hit first in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") after Dave, a Dutch fan, e-mailed Passenger expressing his wish to introduce the song to some Dutch radio stations, claiming it could be a hit there.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) This resulted in the song trending on Dutch stations and finding enormous commercial success with the Dutch public. The song reached number two in the [Dutch Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Top_40 "Dutch Top 40") in November 2012, spending a total of four non-consecutive weeks at that position. The next month that year, it topped at number one.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Netherlands-6)

Since 2013, and after initial success in the Netherlands, "Let Her Go" has reached number one in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"),[\[7\]](#cite_note-Australia-7) [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria"),[\[8\]](#cite_note-Austria-8) [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"),[\[9\]](#cite_note-Vlanders-9) [Czech [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"),[\[12\]](#cite_note-Finland-12) [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"),[\[13\]](#cite_note-Germany-13) [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece"),[\[14\]](#cite_note-Greece-14) [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"),[\[15\]](#cite_note-Ireland-15) [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"),[\[16\]](#cite_note-Israel-16) [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"),[\[17\]](#cite_note-Italy-17) [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"),[\[18\]](#cite_note-Luxembourg-18) [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-Mexico-19) [New Passenger's first international success. The song has sold over 1 million digital copies in the UK,[\[1\]](#cite_note-uksales-1) and over 4 million in the US as of July 2014\.[\[2\]](#cite_note-USSales-2) In October 2019, "Let Her Go" surpassed one billion streams on the music service [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), making it one of the most played songs on the service.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The music video was uploaded on the day after the single, directed and produced by the Australian video artist Dave Jensen and Tavic.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) It shows the stage being prepared for a Passenger concert, with footage of Passenger performance with his backing band and shots of the audience present reacting.

As of June 2026, the video has received over 4 billion views on the video-sharing website [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), making it the [28th most viewed video ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") on the site.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

## Cover versions

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Cover versions")\]

British singer [Birdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdy_\(musician\) "Birdy (musician)") recorded a cover version called "Let Him Go" in 2013 on [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1")'s [Live Lounge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Lounge "Live Lounge").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

An unreleased acoustic version of the song was donated to support college radio in the USA on the 2013 [College Radio Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Radio_Day "College Radio Day") Vol. 2 album. The song was limited to being on only the CD version of the album (only 1,500 copies have been pressed).[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

In August 2014, [Glen Templeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Templeton "Glen Templeton") made a country cover of the song.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

American trance singer [JES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes_\(musician\) "Jes (musician)") released her cover version of the song titled "Let Him Go" in 2019\.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

The song is sampled heavily in [Central Cee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Cee "Central Cee")'s 2022 single "[Let Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_Go_\(Central_Cee_song\) "Let Go (Central Cee song)")".[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

## Confusion with "Let It Go"

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Confusion with \"Let It Go\"")\]

"Let Her Go" is regularly confused with [Idina Menzel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idina_Menzel "Idina Menzel")'s hit song "[Let It Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_It_Go "Let It Go")" from the [Disney Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Animation_Studios "Walt Disney Animation Studios") film *[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_\(2013_film\) "Frozen (2013 film)")*. At the 2018 [Newport Folk Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Folk_Festival "Newport Folk Festival"), Passenger introduced himself to the crowd, then explained: "I've [only had one hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-hit_wonder "One-hit wonder"), so that's a bit embarrassing. And it's called 'Let Her Go', not 'Let It Go' from *Frozen*. Amazing how people get them mixed up. She's a [Disney princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Princess "Disney Princess"), and I'm an Englishman with a beard."[\[36\]](#cite_note-McLean-36) Passenger again joked about the long-running confusion while performing at the [Fox Oakland Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Oakland_Theatre "Fox Oakland Theatre") in September 2024 as part of his Anniversary Tour.[\[37\]](#cite_note-Navale-37)

## In popular culture

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: In popular culture")\]

"Let Her Go" was used in a [Budweiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_\(Anheuser-Busch\) "Budweiser (Anheuser-Busch)") commercial shown during [Super Bowl XLVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVIII "Super Bowl XLVIII") entitled "Puppy Love", which showed the friendship between a [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") puppy and one of the [Budweiser Clydesdales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_Clydesdales "Budweiser Clydesdales").[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) It was used also in the season 7 finale of the Canadian television show *[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_\(Canadian_TV_series\) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")* as the send-off song[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) and in "[500 Years of Solitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/500_Years_of_Solitude "500 Years of Solitude")", the 100th episode of *[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Vampire_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")*.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

Bluegrass band [the Travelin' McCourys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travelin'_McCourys "The Travelin' McCourys") recorded the song at a Nashville studio, [the Butcher Shoppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_R._Ferguson#The_Butcher_Shoppe_Studio "David R. Ferguson") releasing the version on 13 January 2017\.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)

"**Let Her Go**" is a song recorded by English singer-songwriter [Passenger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Passenger_\(singer\) "Passenger (singer)"). It was recorded at [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney")'s [Linear Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_Recording "Linear Recording") and co-produced by Passenger (as Mike Rosenberg) and Chris Vallejo. The recording features Australian musicians Stu Larsen, [Georgia Mooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Mooney "Georgia Mooney"), [Stu Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stu_Hunter "Stu Hunter"), Cameron Undy, and Glenn Wilson. "Let Her Go" was released on 24 July 2012 as the second single from Passenger's fourth album, *[All the Little Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Little_Lights "All the Little Lights")*.

The song became a [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit"), achieving international success and topping the charts in many countries around the world. As of July 2014, it has sold over one million digital copies in the UK, and over four million in the US.[\[1\]](#cite_note-uksales-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-USSales-2) In 2014, the song was nominated for the [Brit Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award "Brit Award") for [British Single of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_BRIT_Awards#Nominees_and_winners "2014 BRIT Awards"), and won Passenger the British Academy's [Ivor Novello Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Award "Ivor Novello Award") for Most Performed Work.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4) In 2023, to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the song, Passenger released a remix version with English singer [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran").

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/89/Passenger.jpg/250px-Passenger.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Passenger.jpg)

Passenger performing "Let Her Go" live in [Bogotá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogotá "Bogotá"), [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") during his [Runaway Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway_Tour_\(Passenger\) "Runaway Tour (Passenger)").

"Let Her Go" was released in July 2012 as the second single from Passenger's third album *[All the Little Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Little_Lights "All the Little Lights")*. The song became a hit first in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") after Dave, a Dutch fan, e-mailed Passenger expressing his wish to introduce the song to some Dutch radio stations, claiming it could be a hit there.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) This resulted in the song trending on Dutch stations and finding enormous commercial success with the Dutch public. The song reached number two in the [Dutch Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_Top_40 "Dutch Top 40") in November 2012, spending a total of four non-consecutive weeks at that position. The next month that year, it topped at number one.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Netherlands-6)

Since 2013, and after initial success in the Netherlands, "Let Her Go" has reached number one in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"),[\[7\]](#cite_note-Australia-7) [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austria "Austria"),[\[8\]](#cite_note-Austria-8) [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"),[\[9\]](#cite_note-Vlanders-9) [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic"),[\[10\]](#cite_note-Czech-10) [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"),[\[11\]](#cite_note-Denmark-11) [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"),[\[12\]](#cite_note-Finland-12) [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"),[\[13\]](#cite_note-Germany-13) [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece"),[\[14\]](#cite_note-Greece-14) [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"),[\[15\]](#cite_note-Ireland-15) [Israel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel "Israel"),[\[16\]](#cite_note-Israel-16) [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"),[\[17\]](#cite_note-Italy-17) [Luxembourg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"),[\[18\]](#cite_note-Luxembourg-18) [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-Mexico-19) [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"),[\[20\]](#cite_note-NewZealand-20) [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"),[\[21\]](#cite_note-Norway-21) [Slovakia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovakia "Slovakia"),[\[22\]](#cite_note-Slovakia-22) [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden")[\[23\]](#cite_note-Sweden-23) and [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Switzerland-24) number two in the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"),[\[25\]](#cite_note-UK-25) number five in the US on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")[\[26\]](#cite_note-US-26) and number one on [*Billboard* Hot Rock Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_number-one_Billboard_Rock_Songs "List of number-one Billboard Rock Songs"),[\[27\]](#cite_note-USRock-27) making it Passenger's first international success. The song has sold over 1 million digital copies in the UK,[\[1\]](#cite_note-uksales-1) and over 4 million in the US as of July 2014\.[\[2\]](#cite_note-USSales-2) In October 2019, "Let Her Go" surpassed one billion streams on the music service [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), making it one of the most played songs on the service.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The music video was uploaded on the day after the single, directed and produced by the Australian video artist Dave Jensen and Tavic.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) It shows the stage being prepared for a Passenger concert, with footage of Passenger performance with his backing band and shots of the audience present reacting.

As of June 2026, the video has received over 4 billion views on the video-sharing website [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), making it the [28th most viewed video ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos") on the site.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

## Cover versions

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Cover versions")\]

British singer [Birdy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdy_\(musician\) "Birdy (musician)") recorded a cover version called "Let Him Go" in 2013 on [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1")'s [Live Lounge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Lounge "Live Lounge").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

An unreleased acoustic version of the song was donated to support college radio in the USA on the 2013 [College Radio Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Radio_Day "College Radio Day") Vol. 2 album. The song was limited to being on only the CD version of the album (only 1,500 copies have been pressed).[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

In August 2014, [Glen Templeton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Templeton "Glen Templeton") made a country cover of the song.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

American trance singer [JES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jes_\(musician\) "Jes (musician)") released her cover version of the song titled "Let Him Go" in 2019\.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34)

The song is sampled heavily in [Central Cee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Cee "Central Cee")'s 2022 single "[Let Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_Go_\(Central_Cee_song\) "Let Go (Central Cee song)")".[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)

## Confusion with "Let It Go"

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Confusion with \"Let It Go\"")\]

"Let Her Go" is regularly confused with [Idina Menzel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idina_Menzel "Idina Menzel")'s hit song "[Let It Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Let_It_Go "Let It Go")" from the [Disney Animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walt_Disney_Animation_Studios "Walt Disney Animation Studios") film *[Frozen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frozen_\(2013_film\) "Frozen (2013 film)")*. At the 2018 [Newport Folk Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Folk_Festival "Newport Folk Festival"), Passenger introduced himself to the crowd, then explained: "I've [only had one hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-hit_wonder "One-hit wonder"), so that's a bit embarrassing. And it's called 'Let Her Go', not 'Let It Go' from *Frozen*. Amazing how people get them mixed up. She's a [Disney princess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Princess "Disney Princess"), and I'm an Englishman with a beard."[\[36\]](#cite_note-McLean-36) Passenger again joked about the long-running confusion while performing at the [Fox Oakland Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Oakland_Theatre "Fox Oakland Theatre") in September 2024 as part of his Anniversary Tour.[\[37\]](#cite_note-Navale-37)

## In popular culture

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Let_Her_Go&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: In popular culture")\]

"Let Her Go" was used in a [Budweiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_\(Anheuser-Busch\) "Budweiser (Anheuser-Busch)") commercial shown during [Super Bowl XLVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLVIII "Super Bowl XLVIII") entitled "Puppy Love", which showed the friendship between a [Labrador Retriever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labrador_Retriever "Labrador Retriever") puppy and one of the [Budweiser Clydesdales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budweiser_Clydesdales "Budweiser Clydesdales").[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) It was used also in the season 7 finale of the Canadian television show *[Heartland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_\(Canadian_TV_series\) "Heartland (Canadian TV series)")* as the send-off song[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) and in "[500 Years of Solitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/500_Years_of_Solitude "500 Years of Solitude")", the 100th episode of *[The Vampire Diaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Vampire_Diaries "The Vampire Diaries")*.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

Bluegrass band [the Travelin' McCourys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Travelin'_McCourys "The Travelin' McCourys") recorded the song at a Nashville studio, [the Butcher Shoppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_R._Ferguson#The_Butcher_Shoppe_Studio "David R. Ferguson") releasing the version on 13 January 2017\.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)

"**Treat You Better**" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter [Shawn Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes "Shawn Mendes"), released through [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") on June 3, 2016, as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his second studio album, *[Illuminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_\(Shawn_Mendes_album\) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")* (2016).[\[3\]](#cite_note-iTunes_Store_\(US\)-3) It was co-written by Mendes with [Teddy Geiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Geiger "Teddy Geiger"), and [Scott Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Harris_\(songwriter\) "Scott Harris (songwriter)"), while Geiger produced the song alongside [Dan Romer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Romer "Dan Romer"), and Daylight. The music video was released on July 12, 2016, and features a storyline about an abusive relationship.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

"Treat You Better" peaked at number six on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming his second top ten on the chart. Elsewhere, the song has topped charts in Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia, and peaked within the top ten of the record charts in Canada, the United Kingdom and 18 other countries.

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Composition")\]

The song is written in the key of [B♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor").[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) and has a tempo of 83 beats per minute.

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Treat You Better" at number 42 on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*'s [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") named it the eighth best song of the year.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The music video was released on July 12, 2016\.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It features a plot revolving around a situation of violence between couples. The video shows a girl being abused by her boyfriend in various situations, while Mendes hopes to be with her and struggles to understand why she prefers to be in that relationship. The video ends displaying the number for the [National Domestic Violence Hotline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Domestic_Violence_Hotline "National Domestic Violence Hotline").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The music video also stars [Devon Aoki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devon_Aoki "Devon Aoki")'s half sister Ellie Stuart Hunter [\[10\]](#cite_note-10) played with a guitar, drums and tambourines.

The video has received over 2\.5 billion YouTube views as of July 2025,[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) and is one of the site's 100 [most-watched videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

On the issue dating June 25, 2016, the song debuted at number thirty four on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) and would later peak at number six on October 8, 2016, making it Mendes' second top 10 single. It also reached the top 10 on the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") and [Adult Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Top_40 "Adult Top 40") national airplay charts. In Canada, the song has peaked at number seven on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), passing "[Life of the Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_of_the_Party_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\) "Life of the Party (Shawn Mendes song)")" as his highest-peaking single in his home country. The song has additionally achieved a top 5 position on the national [CHR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_CHR/Top_40 "Canada CHR/Top 40") and [Hot AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_Hot_AC "Canada Hot AC") airplay charts, and has been certified gold by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada"). "Treat You Better" has also reached the top 10 in multiple markets including Australia, Germany, and Sweden.

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Mendes' first televised performance of "Treat You Better" happened at the [2016 Much Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_iHeartRadio_Much_Music_Video_Awards "2016 iHeartRadio Much Music Video Awards") on June 19\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) On July 12, 2016, he performed the song on *[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*,[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) and again on October 8, 2018, with [Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fallon "Jimmy Fallon") and his house band The Roots as backing using "classroom instruments".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

"**Treat You Better**" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter [Shawn Mendes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Mendes "Shawn Mendes"), released through [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records") on June 3, 2016, as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from his second studio album, *[Illuminate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illuminate_\(Shawn_Mendes_album\) "Illuminate (Shawn Mendes album)")* (2016).[\[3\]](#cite_note-iTunes_Store_\(US\)-3) It was co-written by Mendes with [Teddy Geiger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Geiger "Teddy Geiger"), and [Scott Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Harris_\(songwriter\) "Scott Harris (songwriter)"), while Geiger produced the song alongside [Dan Romer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Romer "Dan Romer"), and Daylight. The music video was released on July 12, 2016, and features a storyline about an abusive relationship.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)

"Treat You Better" peaked at number six on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), becoming his second top ten on the chart. Elsewhere, the song has topped charts in Poland, Slovakia and Slovenia, and peaked within the top ten of the record charts in Canada, the United Kingdom and 18 other countries.

## Composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Composition")\]

The song is written in the key of [B♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor").[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) and has a tempo of 83 beats per minute.

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

*[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")* ranked "Treat You Better" at number 42 on their "100 Best Pop Songs of 2016" list.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*'s [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") named it the eighth best song of the year.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

The music video was released on July 12, 2016\.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) It features a plot revolving around a situation of violence between couples. The video shows a girl being abused by her boyfriend in various situations, while Mendes hopes to be with her and struggles to understand why she prefers to be in that relationship. The video ends displaying the number for the [National Domestic Violence Hotline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Domestic_Violence_Hotline "National Domestic Violence Hotline").[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) The music video also stars [Devon Aoki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devon_Aoki "Devon Aoki")'s half sister Ellie Stuart Hunter [\[10\]](#cite_note-10) played with a guitar, drums and tambourines.

The video has received over 2\.5 billion YouTube views as of July 2025,[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) and is one of the site's 100 [most-watched videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most-viewed_YouTube_videos "List of most-viewed YouTube videos").[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

## Chart performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Chart performance")\]

On the issue dating June 25, 2016, the song debuted at number thirty four on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100")[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) and would later peak at number six on October 8, 2016, making it Mendes' second top 10 single. It also reached the top 10 on the [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") and [Adult Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Top_40 "Adult Top 40") national airplay charts. In Canada, the song has peaked at number seven on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), passing "[Life of the Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_of_the_Party_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\) "Life of the Party (Shawn Mendes song)")" as his highest-peaking single in his home country. The song has additionally achieved a top 5 position on the national [CHR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_CHR/Top_40 "Canada CHR/Top 40") and [Hot AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada_Hot_AC "Canada Hot AC") airplay charts, and has been certified gold by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada"). "Treat You Better" has also reached the top 10 in multiple markets including Australia, Germany, and Sweden.

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Treat_You_Better_\(Shawn_Mendes_song\)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Mendes' first televised performance of "Treat You Better" happened at the [2016 Much Music Video Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_iHeartRadio_Much_Music_Video_Awards "2016 iHeartRadio Much Music Video Awards") on June 19\.[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) On July 12, 2016, he performed the song on *[The Tonight Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*,[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) and again on October 8, 2018, with [Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Fallon "Jimmy Fallon") and his house band The Roots as backing using "classroom instruments".[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

# Shawn Mendes’s ‘Treat You Better’ Video Is A Reminder That No One Has To Tolerate Abuse

The *Illuminate* visual speaks out for victims of domestic violence

by [Sasha Geffen](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/http://www.mtv.com/news/author/sashageffens/ "Posts by Sasha Geffen") 7/12/2016

[Shawn Mendes](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/http://www.mtv.com/artists/shawn-mendes/)’s new single “Treat You Better” is an archetypal entry into the genre of jealousy songs, but its video takes his message one step further.

In his new clip, Mendes pines over a girl who’s stuck in an abusive relationship with another guy. Even though her boyfriend throws her around when they fight, she sticks with him — much to the dismay of Mendes, who’s hoping to be with her instead and hits a few walls about it.  

Embedded from [www.youtube.com](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/https://www.youtube.com/embed/lY2yjAdbvdQ?feature=oembed).

  
The dramatic video ends by displaying the number for the National Domestic Violence Hotline, implicitly encouraging anyone who’s in an abusive relationship (or knows someone who is) to seek out help.

# Shawn Mendes’s ‘Treat You Better’ Video Is A Reminder That No One Has To Tolerate Abuse

The *Illuminate* visual speaks out for victims of domestic violence

by [Sasha Geffen](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/http://www.mtv.com/news/author/sashageffens/ "Posts by Sasha Geffen") 7/12/2016

[Shawn Mendes](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/http://www.mtv.com/artists/shawn-mendes/)’s new single “Treat You Better” is an archetypal entry into the genre of jealousy songs, but its video takes his message one step further.

In his new clip, Mendes pines over a girl who’s stuck in an abusive relationship with another guy. Even though her boyfriend throws her around when they fight, she sticks with him — much to the dismay of Mendes, who’s hoping to be with her instead and hits a few walls about it.  

Embedded from [www.youtube.com](https://web.archive.org/web/20160715061926/https://www.youtube.com/embed/lY2yjAdbvdQ?feature=oembed).

  
The dramatic video ends by displaying the number for the National Domestic Violence Hotline, implicitly encouraging anyone who’s in an abusive relationship (or knows someone who is) to seek out help.

All evidence converges. Here's my final analysis:

## Summary

**Barcode profile** (250 stripes ≈ 1s each; durations all fit ~230–290s): extremely dark (mean luminance 26.6, 57% of stripes near-black), warm brown/amber throughout, no green, no bright white scenes — with distinctive dark-blue stripes at 0%, 3%, 7%, 36%, 50–54%, 87–88%, deep-red stripes at 51–54%, one bright gray-white flash at ~32%, and a long, steady warm-brown finale (~89–98.5%) fading to black.

**Eliminations:**
- **F, E, B, H, C** (Shake It Off, Girls Like You, Attention, Bad Romance, What Do You Mean?) — all bright/neon/white-heavy videos; the barcode is 96% dark. ❌
- **D (Rolling in the Deep)** — its three auto-keyframes are all bright gray-white plaster-wall scenes (lum ~70), contradicting a barcode that's near-black almost everywhere. ❌
- **J (Counting Stars)** — keyframes are mid-bright and *greenish* (fluorescent-lit room); the barcode has zero green anywhere. ❌
- **G (Thinking Out Loud)** — bright grand-hall dance video, mid-tone golds/whites, no dark-blue or deep-red scenes. ❌

**Finalists: A (Let Her Go) vs. I (Treat You Better)** — both dark, warm videos:
- Keyframe comparison at 25/50/75% of runtime: Passenger's live-stage keyframes are bright amber (lum ~43) at 25% and 50% where the barcode is near-black — total color distance **232**. Shawn Mendes' keyframes are dark warm (total distance **142**), matching at every point.
- Decisive: TYB's halfway keyframe is literally the **couple in a car at night** — exactly where the barcode shows alternating **dark blue (streetlight glow) and dark red (taillights)** stripes, colors a consistently amber-lit concert video like Let Her Go can't produce. TYB's gritty abusive-relationship narrative also explains the repeated near-black stretches (dark apartment fights, night scenes), the blue night shots at 0%/87–88%, and the steady warm loft ending followed by the black domestic-violence-hotline card at the very end.
- Duration: 257s ≈ 250 stripes × ~1s ✓

Answer: I
